title: H.B. 4098 — Artificial intelligence business; attorney general
mechanism: An artificial intelligence business shall conduct a comprehensive risk assessment for each high risk AI system before using or selling it, including assessing catastrophic risks. It shall submit a transparency report to the attorney general before using or selling a high risk AI system, and the reports shall be publicly posted on its website. It shall conduct a quarterly audit. The attorney general shall issue a certification before an artificial intelligence business enters the stream of commerce.
thresholds: Frontier model: trained using greater than 10.26 computational operations to compute costs of more than $100,000,000, or by applying knowledge distillation to a frontier model. Large developer: spent more than $5,000,000 in developing and more than $100,000,000 in training a frontier model.
penalties: Attorney general enforces; may impose a civil penalty of not more than $50,000 per violation; each day a violation occurs constitutes a separate violation. A business that implements recognized standards for and complies with the children's online privacy protection act of 1998 advisory services may receive a reduced civil penalty for inadvertent violations.

framework.summary: The bill does not require a published safety or risk-management framework; it requires risk assessments and audits.

transparency_report.summary: An AI business must submit a transparency report to the attorney general before using or selling a high risk AI system, and post the reports publicly on its website.
transparency_report.quote:
An artificial intelligence
business shall submit a transparency report to the attorney general before
using or selling a high risk AI system.

incident_reporting.summary: The bill has no requirement to report safety incidents to a government body.

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no shorter reporting window for imminent risks.

third_party_audit.summary: The bill requires the business to run its own quarterly audit but does not require an independent or third-party audit or evaluation.

whistleblower.summary: The bill has no employee protections.

registration.summary: The bill has no registration, licensing or notification requirement for the business; the attorney general's certification is not a registration duty.

shutdown.summary: The bill has no shutdown or kill-switch requirement.

compute_threshold.summary: A frontier model is defined as one trained using greater than 10.26 computational operations at compute costs of more than $100,000,000, or by distillation of a frontier model.
